Abstract
Linguistic uses
This article explores the linguistic uses in the play (John Okello’s Sacrifice). The linguistic elements encompass all the fundamental contents used in literary works. The use of language is considered one of the artistic aspects of a literary work, and art contains all the essential components employed to create a literary piece, such as themes, characters, structure, style, and title. In the aspect of language use, critics examine these features—expressions, metaphors, foreign languages, and so on—depending on the critic's objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the drama Sacrifice by director John Okello (2015). The play was written by the Tanzanian author Emmanuel Mbujo. It is a play about the revolution of the Zanzibar government that took place in 1964. Here, the researcher relied on analyzing the use of language in this literary work. Literature is a branch of art that uses spoken language or text to convey a message to society. In order for the intended message to reach the community, it is important for authors to use language creatively in conveying the message to the audience. Emmanuel Mbogo, who resides in mainland Tanzania, presents a drama about the people of Zanzibar (Unguja and Pemba). The expressions given to all the characters in this work correspond to the large percentage of the islands’ population. A language is assigned to each character to suit their role. All the elements used may have carried different intentions, but unfortunately the researcher did not utilize them. The elements of language used aimed to conceptualize the various themes in this drama. Certainly, the foundations of structuralist theory have been considered regarding the use of language in the literary work of this drama.

“Art as Technique” states that for a writer to effectively convey their emotions in literature, it is necessary for those emotions to be constructed in a way that presents novelty to the readers or listeners by utilizing elements of language use (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006). Elements of language use include sayings, figures of speech, imagery, and the use of foreign or indigenous languages that are distinct from the literary work itself. He adds by saying that the innovation of one period is different from the innovation of another period. This means that innovation in literary works must constantly change depending on the audience, subject, context, and time, which prevents the literary work from becoming routine and instead gives it renewed vitality each time it is engaged. Shklovisky emphasizes the concept of innovation by stating that it is not about changing the meaning but rather about the manner or way of expressing something. Introduction  
The use of language is one of the aspects found in the external structure of a literary work, that is, its form. Form encompasses all the essential elements used to shape a literary work, such as setting, characters, structure, style, and the title of the work/anthology, among others. In examining the use of language, critics focus on these elements: expressions, figures of speech, register, foreign languages, etc., depending on the critic’s objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the play *John Okello’s Sacrifice* (2015). This play was written by Emmanuel Mbogo, a literary writer from Tanzania. It is a play that discusses the Zanzibar Revolution, which took place in 1964. The theory of Formalism will guide our discussion. This theory is primarily focused on analyzing the use of language in literary works. Proponents of this theory believe that every literary work employs this approach, as it deals with a fundamental aspect of this branch of art—language, which is the main pillar of literature. In this play, we will identify various elements of language use, guided by the theory of Formalism. 1.1 The Theory of Formalism  
Schmitz (2007) and Carter (2006) have outlined several ideas of formalist theorists as follows: distinguishing between the use of ordinary language and literary language, they believed and emphasized that the concept of innovation or novelty is the main function of art, and they preferred literary criticism to have a scientific orientation; thus, they sought to establish scientific approaches in literature.  
According to the ideas of the formalists, all literary works utilize this theory because a work cannot be considered literary if it does not possess artistic qualities. These artistic qualities involve the construction of language elements that demonstrate the novelty of the work. Therefore, anyone who critiques any literary work based on the theory of Formalism will inevitably have to confront the issue of "novelty"—that is, the features that construct the use of language are unavoidable. The theory of Formalism is among the theories that analyze and explain the use of language in the disciplines of literature and linguistics. This theory originated from activists in two academic circles in Russia: on the one hand, the linguists of the Moscow Linguistics Circle, and on the other, the Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), both aiming to bring revolutions to linguistics and literary criticism (Schmitz, 2007). In conclusion, the theory of Formalism has greatly contributed to the advancement and development of literary criticism. This contribution stems from the concept of innovation or novelty in literary works, the challenges and various debates it has sparked, which have generated diverse knowledge and ideas within the field of literature, as well as the emergence of other theories such as the theory of Modernism. 1.2 The Use of Language in the Play “John Okello’s Sacrifice”

These are words used to emphasize or stress a particular issue. This technique is most evident in the genre of poetry, although it also appears in other genres (Mulokozi 1999). Repetition can appear through the recurrence of a word, rhythm, refrain, or rhyme. In the selected play, John Okello's Sacrifice, this figure of speech has been used. The author has used the following repetitions;
ASHURA: “Today! “Today!” Today at what time… (p.14)
This is a figure of speech used to attribute human actions to non-human entities, giving an inanimate thing the ability to act as a human does. On page six of the selected play, the character RASHID is used to illustrate this figure of personification. Rashid says,
“Is it that I have no mother, that the baobab tree split, and I was born?” (p.6)
Repetition appears in the use of the word ‘today’ in the statement by the character Ashura. This character uses the word to convey emphasis. He wants his companion to specify exactly at what time today he will finish what he is talking about, since today has many hours. 1.2.6 Semantics  
The baobab is a plant. The way plants reproduce is different from how human beings are born. In this statement by RASHID, this plant is given the attribute of giving birth like a human being. This personification has been used to provoke reflection among the colonizers who were oppressing the inhabitants of Zanzibar, urging them to also respect these Black people who were born like other human beings. Mulokozi (1996) states that sayings are short expressions that carry deep meaning within them. In Swahili oral literature, it is claimed that sayings are the result of long life experiences that the elders went through, which is why they often appear to be true whenever they are quoted. In this genre, there are various subgenres such as proverbs, riddles, idioms, and sayings. Proverbs have been used in this selected play. OKELLO: Whatever has a beginning, has an end (p.17)

In this figure of speech, the words used have a meaning completely different from the intended meaning. It requires the audience to think deeply in order to discern the intended meaning. The author has also used this figure of speech in this selected play. For example,

The three people referred to here by the character Okello have had their level of performance greatly diminished. It has been reduced so much that it can be compared to the pace of a tortoise, which is known to be extremely slow, in words that cannot be uttered. Indeed, this is irony or sarcasm directed at the intended recipients of this statement. They are being reminded to do things more quickly. 1.2.4 Satire  
This is a figure of speech characterized by intense derision (Senkoro 1981). The words that are heard are completely different from the intended meaning. One character, BIBI, has been used by the author to represent this figure of speech in the selected play.  
BIBI: ...Has the God you worship become your uncle?... This proverb, "Unity is strength and division is weakness," is used to encourage unity among members of the community. It emphasizes that people should stick together in whatever they set out to do. The author uses this proverb through the character Okello as he encourages his fellow youths to go to war in order to stage a revolution and ultimately attain true freedom in their land. The last two proverbs, "A donkey’s gratitude is a kick" and "Patience ends up eating what is spoiled," reflect the regret experienced by the main character of this play, John Okello. This main character made a significant contribution to the liberation of various countries in Africa (including Zanzibar), but was not remembered anywhere. Every time he completed a liberation struggle, he was expelled and ended up in prison. The author has used the technique of irony, stating the proverb in reverse; instead of saying “Patience ends up eating what is ripe,” he wrote “Patience ends up eating what is spoiled.” All this was to express the sorrow of this character, Okello. 1.2.7 Idioms  
The character BIBI poses a question to people who appear to worship God every day, yet their actions are filled with oppression and severe injustice. The deeds they commit do not reflect the teachings of Almighty God. They persecute people, slaves, and anyone else who crosses their path who does not share their skin color. This question is indeed satire directed at those who appear to fear God while committing evil deeds. The author says, God is not to be mocked, deceived, or manipulated. These are brief statements that are used by society to emphasize the truth of a particular matter. It is said that such statements connect different concepts or ideas into a single point with the aim of conveying the intended message. Ifuatayo ni orodha ya kurasa zetu maarufu zaidi nchini Marekani (2015). Mazungumzo na mashairi kwa Kiingereza pamoja na tafsiri yake ya Kiingereza. Dunha ni tamthilia inayohusu mapinduzi ya serikali ya Zanzibar, yaliyotokea mwaka 1964, ambapo mtafiti alilenga kuchambua matumizi ya lugha katika kazi hii ya fasihi. Fasihi ni tawi la sanaa linalotumia lugha ya mazungumzo au maandishi kufikisha ujumbe kwa jamii. Ili ujumbe uliokusudiwa uwafikie wanajamii, ni wazo zuri kwa waandishi kutumia lugha kwa ubunifu katika uwasilishaji wa ujumbe kwa hadhira. Emmanuel Mbogo, ambaye yuko Tanzania Bara, anasema kwamba tamthilia hii inawahusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Makala hii inachunguza matumizi ya lugha katika tamthilia (Sadaka ya John Okello). Vipengele vya lugha vinahusisha maudhui yote ya msingi yanayotumika katika kazi za fasihi. Matumizi ya lugha yanachukuliwa kuwa mojawapo ya mambo ya kisanii katika kazi ya fasihi, na sanaa inajumuisha vipengele vyote muhimu vinavyotumiwa kuunda kazi ya fasihi, kama vile mada, wahusika, muundo, mtindo na kichwa. Katika kipengele cha matumizi ya lugha, wakosoaji hukagua sifa hizi—mwenendo wa usemi, tamathali za semi, lugha za kigeni, na kadhalika—kulingana na lengo la mkosoaji. Katika makala hii, tunachunguza matumizi ya lugha katika tamthilia Sadaka iliyoongozwa na John Okello (2015). Tamthilia hii iliandikwa na mwandishi wa Kitanzania Emmanuel Mbujo. Ni tamthilia kuhusu mapinduzi ya serikali ya Zanzibar yaliyotokea mwaka 1964. Hapa, mtafiti alitegemea kuchambua matumizi ya lugha katika kazi hii ya fasihi. Ili ujumbe unaokusudiwa uweze kuwafikia wanajamii, ni muhimu kwa waandishi kutumia lugha kwa ubunifu katika kufikisha ujumbe kwa hadhira. Emmanuel Mbogo, ambaye anaishi Tanzania Bara, anawasilisha tamthilia kuhusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Mwenendo wa usemi uliotolewa kwa wahusika wote katika kazi hii unalingana na asilimia kubwa ya wakazi wa visiwa. Lugha imetolewa kwa kila mhusika ili iendane na nafasi yake. Vipengele vyote vilivyotumiwa huenda vilikuwa na madhumuni mbalimbali, lakini kwa bahati mbaya mtafiti hakuvitumia. Vipengele vya lugha vilivyotumiwa vililenga kuelezea mada mbalimbali katika tamthilia hii. Hakika, misingi ya nadharia ya muundo imezingatiwa kuhusu matumizi ya lugha katika kazi ya fasihi ya tamthilia hii.

“Insha kama Mbinu” inabainisha kwamba ili mwandishi aweze kufikisha hisia zake kikamilifu katika fasihi, ni muhimu hisia hizo zijengwe kwa namna inayowapa usomaji au usikilizaji kitu kipya kupitia matumizi ya vipengele vya lugha (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006). Vipengele vya matumizi ya lugha vinajumuisha misemo, tamathali za semi, taswira, na matumizi ya lugha za kigeni au za asili zinazoibuka tofauti na kazi yenyewe ya fasihi. Anaongeza kwa kusema kwamba ubunifu wa kipindi kimoja ni tofauti na ubunifu wa kipindi kingine. Hii ina maana kwamba ubunifu katika kazi za fasihi lazima ubadilike mara kwa mara kulingana na hadhira, mada, muktadha, na wakati, jambo linalozuia kazi ya fasihi kuwa ya mazoea tu na badala yake kuitia uhai mpya kila inaposhughulikiwa. Shklovisky anasisitiza dhana ya ubunifu kwa kusema kwamba si suala la kubadili maana, bali ni juu ya namna au njia ya kueleza jambo fulani. Utangulizi  
Matumizi ya lugha ni mojawapo ya mambo yanayopatikana katika muundo wa nje wa kazi ya fasihi, yaani umbo lake. Umbo linajumuisha vipengele vyote muhimu vinavyotumiwa kuunda kazi ya fasihi, kama vile muktadha, wahusika, muundo, mtindo, na kichwa cha kazi/antolojia, pamoja na mambo mengine. Katika kuchunguza matumizi ya lugha, wakosoaji huzingatia vipengele hivi: usemi, tamathali za semi, rejista, lugha za kigeni, n.k., kulingana na madhumuni ya mkosoaji. Katika makala hii, tunachunguza matumizi ya lugha katika tamthilia ya *Sadaka ya John Okello* (2015). Tamthilia hii iliandikwa na Emmanuel Mbogo, mwandishi wa fasihi kutoka Tanzania. Ni tamthilia inayojadili mapinduzi ya serikali ya Zanzibar yaliyotokea mwaka 1964. Nadharia ya Uformali itatuongoza katika mjadala wetu. Nadharia hii inajikita hasa katika kuchunguza matumizi ya lugha katika kazi za fasihi. Wanazuoni wa nadharia hii wanaamini kuwa kila kazi ya fasihi hutumia mbinu hii, kwani inajihusisha na kipengele cha msingi cha tawi hili la sanaa—lugha, ambayo ndiyo nguzo kuu ya fasihi. Katika tamthilia hii, tutaainisha vipengele mbalimbali vya matumizi ya lugha, tukiongozwa na nadharia ya Uformali. 1.1 Nadharia ya Uformali  
Schmitz (2007) na Carter (2006) wameelezea mawazo kadhaa ya wananadharia wa uformali kama ifuatavyo: kutofautisha kati ya matumizi ya lugha ya kawaida na lugha ya kifasihi, waliamini na kusisitiza kwamba dhana ya ubunifu au jambo jipya ndiyo kazi kuu ya sanaa, na walipendelea uchambuzi wa fasihi uwe na mwelekeo wa kisayansi; kwa hivyo, walilenga kuweka mbinu za kisayansi ndani ya fasihi.  
Kwa mujibu wa mawazo ya waformali, kazi zote za fasihi hutumia nadharia hii kwa sababu kazi haiwezi kuchukuliwa kuwa ya kifasihi kama haina sifa za kisanii. Sifa hizi za kisanii zinahusisha uundaji wa vipengele vya lugha vinavyoonyesha ubunifu wa kazi hiyo. Hivyo, mtu yeyote anayechambua kazi yoyote ya fasihi kwa msingi wa Nadharia ya Uformali hatakosa kukutana na suala la “ubunifu”—yaani, mambo yanayojenga matumizi ya lugha hayaepukiki. Nadharia ya Uformali ni miongoni mwa nadharia zinazochambua na kufafanua matumizi ya lugha katika taaluma za fasihi na isimu. Nadharia hii ilianzia kwa wanaharakati wa vikundi viwili vya kitaaluma nchini Urusi: kwa upande mmoja, wasomi wa Isimu kutoka Mduara wa Isimu wa Moscow, na kwa upande mwingine, Jumuiya ya Utafiti wa Lugha ya Ushairi (OPAYAZ), vyote vikilenga kuleta mapinduzi katika isimu na uchambuzi wa fasihi (Schmitz, 2007). Kwa kumalizia, nadharia ya Uformali imechangia kwa kiasi kikubwa katika ustawi na maendeleo ya ukosoaji wa fasihi. Mchango huu unatokana na dhana ya ubunifu au jipya katika kazi za fasihi, changamoto na mijadala mbalimbali ilizozusha, ambazo zimesababisha kujitokeza kwa maarifa na mawazo tofauti tofauti katika uwanja wa fasihi, pamoja na kujitokeza kwa nadharia nyingine kama vile nadharia ya Uhamiaji wa Kisasa (Modernism). 1.2 Matumizi ya Lugha katika Tamthilia ya "Sadaka ya John Okello"  
1.2.1 Sitiari  
Hii ni tamathali ya semi inayounga vitu viwili au zaidi ambavyo vinafanana kwa namna fulani. Maneno yanayotumiwa zaidi katika tamathali hii ya semi ni kama vile: kama, mithili ya, sawa na, mfano wa, miongoni mwa mengine. Katika tamthilia yetu iliyochaguliwa, tamathali hii ya semi imejitokeza katika sehemu nyingi. Mwandishi wetu Emmanuel Mbogo amejitahidi kutumia kila tukio kulingana na mazungumzo ya wahusika wake. Sitiari zifuatazo zinajitokeza:
“…Uhuru wa Zanzibar unanukia kama manukato ya Pemba…” (uk.1)
Wengi wa wanaharakati hawa walikuwa vijana ambao walijuana na walikuwa na mazoea na kila mmoja, kwani waliweza kujadiliana pamoja huku wakikubaliana na kutokubaliana kwenye baadhi ya mawazo. Walikuwa na motisha na hamasa ya kuanzisha maarifa ya kitaaluma kwa njia yoyote, ikiwemo kupitia mijadala. Katika mijadala yao, walijitambulisha kama waformali wakiwa na lengo la kuleta mapinduzi katika nyanja ya utafiti wa kisomi. Waliweza pia kufanya maandamano katika miji ya St. Petersburg na Moscow kabla ya mapinduzi ya mwaka 1917. Kutokana na juhudi za wanaharakati hawa, waliweza kufichua mambo mbalimbali ya utamaduni wa Urusi kama vile muziki, sanaa, fasihi, na isimu. Wakati wa kipindi cha machafuko na vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe, wafuasi wa uanasoshalisti (formalisti) walipiga hatua katika kudai haki zao, lakini walizuiwa na wafuasi wa ukomunisti ambao walidai walikuwa wanatenda kinyume na misingi ya uhalisia wa ujamaa (socialist realism). Wanaformali walijaribu kuelezea itikadi zao, lakini hawakufanikiwa, na mwaka 1930 jambo hili lilipelekea kuvunjwa kwa kundi la wanaformali nchini Urusi. Licha ya kuvunjika huko, mawazo yao yaliendelezwa na baadhi ya wanaformalisti kama Victor Shklovsky, Roman Jakobson, na wengine katika uwanja wa fasihi na wasomi wengine nje ya Urusi. “Kama nahodha wa meli!” (uk.4)  
“Kama rubani wa ndege!” (uk.4)  
“Kama kamanda wa jeshi” (uk.4)  
Katika kauli zilizotolewa kwa wahusika hawa, tashbihi “kama” inaonekana. Katika sehemu ya kwanza, uhuru wa Zanzibar umefananishwa na manukato ya Pemba. Hakuna shaka kwamba wazawa wa Zanzibar walikuwa na shauku kubwa ya kupata uhuru kutoka kwa wakoloni; dalili zilipoanza kuonekana kwamba huenda wangeupata, waliufananisha na manukato ya Pemba, ambayo yanachukuliwa kuwa kivutio na wakazi wa huko.

Waformalist walitambulisha dhana kuu mbili katika fasihi: ya kwanza ni ile ya mazoea, na ya pili ni ile ya kufanya jambo lionekane geni. Kulingana na Carter (2006), dhana ya ile ya mazoea hutokea pale kitu kinapotumiwa mara kwa mara hadi kinakuwa cha kawaida kabisa. Katika fasihi, ile ya mazoea inaweza kutokea iwapo msomaji au msikilizaji ataiona kazi ya fasihi kama ya kawaida na kushindwa kuitofautisha na kazi isiyo ya fasihi (ya kawaida). Hii hutokana na kusikia au kusoma kazi hiyo mara kwa mara. Kulingana na dhana hii ya mazoea, Shklovsky alianzisha wazo jingine—ubunifu au jipya katika kazi za fasihi—katika makala yake katika JOHS Juz.20 Na. Utani wa kejeli, kama ambavyo mtu anaweza kuonyesha kwa mjomba wake mwenyewe. 1.2.5 Marudio/Shada  
Kwenye kisiwa cha Unguja. Pia katika uk. Mwandishi amemfananishia Sultani Jamshid na vitu mbalimbali, kama vile nahodha wa meli, rubani wa ndege, na kamanda wa jeshi. Neno "kama" limetumika kufanya ulinganisho huu katika tamthilia ya *Sadaka ya John Okello*. 1.2.2 Uhuishaji  
Haya ni maneno yanayotumika kusisitiza au kutilia mkazo suala fulani. Mbinu hii inaonekana zaidi katika tanzu ya ushairi, ingawa pia inajitokeza katika tanzu nyingine (Mulokozi 1999). Marudio yanaweza kujitokeza kupitia kurudiwa kwa neno, mpangilio wa mizani, kibwagizo, au mizani ya vina. Katika tamthilia iliyochaguliwa, Sadaka ya John Okello, tamathali hii ya usemi imetumika. Mwandishi ametumia marudio yafuatayo;
ASHURA: “Leo! “Leo!” Leo saa ngapi… (uk.14)
Hii ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kutoa sifa za kibinadamu kwa vitu visivyo na uhai, na hivyo kutoa uwezo kwa kitu kisicho na uhai kutenda kama mwanadamu. Kwenye ukurasa wa sita wa tamthilia iliyochaguliwa, mhusika RASHID anatumika kuonesha tamathali hii ya uhuishaji. Rashid anasema,
"Je, ni kwamba sina mama, kwamba mti wa mbuyu ulipasuka, nami nikazaliwa?" (uk.6)
Marudio yanaonekana katika matumizi ya neno ‘leo’ kwenye kauli ya mhusika Ashura. Mhusika huyu anatumia neno hilo kusisitiza. Anataka mwenzake aeleze kwa uwazi kabisa saa ngapi leo atamaliza kile anachokizungumzia, kwa kuwa leo kuna masaa mengi. 1.2.6 Semantiki  
Mbuyu ni mmea. Njia ambayo mimea huzaliana ni tofauti na jinsi binadamu wanavyozaliwa. Katika kauli hii ya RASHID, mmea huu umepewa sifa ya kujifungua kama binadamu. Uhuishaji huu umetumika kuchochea tafakari miongoni mwa wakoloni waliokuwa wakiwakandamiza wakazi wa Zanzibar, ukiwasukuma pia kuwaheshimu watu hawa Weusi ambao walizaliwa kama wanadamu wengine. Mulokozi (1996) anasema kwamba methali ni misemo mifupi inayobeba maana nzito ndani yake. Katika fasihi simulizi ya Kiswahili, inadaiwa kuwa methali ni matokeo ya uzoefu wa maisha marefu ambao wazee walipitia, ndiyo sababu mara nyingi huonekana kuwa na ukweli kila zinaponukuliwa. Katika tanzu hii, kuna tanzu ndogo mbalimbali kama vile methali, vitendawili, nahau na misemo. Methali zimetumika katika tamthiliya hii iliyochaguliwa. Aina hii ya msemo ina sehemu mbili: sehemu ya kwanza inaeleza kitu fulani, na sehemu ya pili inaeleza matokeo yake. Emmanuel Mbogo ametumia methali hizi;  
Vivyo hivyo, kwenye ukurasa wa 3 mwandishi anasema, “Historia iliyoshika alizeti au waridi.” Uwezo wa kushika au kumiliki kitu ni wa wanadamu. Wanadamu hushika vitu kwa mikono yao. Katika kauli hii, mwandishi anaupa historia uwezo wa kibinadamu, akionyesha kwamba historia inashikilia, kuhifadhi na kulinda mambo yenye thamani kubwa zaidi. Alizeti na waridi zimetumika kuakisi mambo mema na mazuri yanayovutia katika jamii. RAMADHANI: …Umoja ni nguvu na utengano ni udhaifu (uk.10)  
1.2.3 Tashtiti au Mzaha  
OKELLO: Kila lenye mwanzo lina mwisho (uk.17)  
RASHIDI: …Ni dua tu ya kuku isiyomwogopesha mwewe… (uk.17)  
Katika tamathali hii ya usemi, maneno yaliyotumika yana maana tofauti kabisa na ile iliyokusudiwa. Inahitaji ihadhira kufikiri kwa kina ili kubaini maana iliyokusudiwa. Mwandishi pia ametumia tamathali hii ya semi katika tamthilia hii iliyochaguliwa. Kwa mfano,  
OKELLO: Shukrani ya punda ni teke. (uk.67)
OKELLO: …wote watatu wana mwendo wa kobe…(uk.10)
Subira hula vilivyooza. (uk.68)
Watu watatu wanaorejelewa hapa na mhusika Okello wamepungua sana katika kiwango chao cha utendaji. Imepunguzwa sana kiasi kwamba inaweza kulinganishwa na mwendo wa kobe, ambaye anajulikana kwa kuwa wa polepole sana, kwa maneno yasiyoweza kusemwa. Hakika, hii ni kejeli au dhihaka iliyolengwa kwa walengwa wa kauli hii. Wanakumbushwa kufanya mambo kwa haraka zaidi. 1.2.4 Udhihaki  
Hii ni sitiari inayojulikana kwa kejeli kali (Senkoro 1981). Maneno yanayosikika ni tofauti kabisa na maana iliyokusudiwa. Mhusika mmoja, BIBI, ametumiwa na mwandishi kuwakilisha tamathali hii ya semi katika tamthilia iliyochaguliwa.  
BIBI: ...Je, Mungu unayemwabudu amekuwa mjomba wako?... Methali hii, "Umoja ni nguvu na utengano ni udhaifu," hutumika kuhimiza umoja miongoni mwa wanajamii. Inasisitiza kwamba watu wanapaswa kushikamana katika jambo lolote wanalolikusudia kufanya. Mwandishi anatumia methali hii kupitia kwa mhusika Okello anapowahamasisha vijana wenzake waende vitani ili kufanya mapinduzi na hatimaye kupata uhuru wa kweli katika nchi yao. Methali mbili za mwisho, "Shukrani ya punda ni teke" na "Subira hulamba wali uliolowa," zinaakisi majuto yaliyompata mhusika mkuu wa tamthilia hii, John Okello. Mhusika mkuu huyu alichangia pakubwa katika ukombozi wa nchi mbalimbali barani Afrika (ikiwemo Zanzibar), lakini hakukumbukwa popote. Kila mara alipomaliza mapambano ya ukombozi, alifukuzwa na kuishia gerezani. Mwandishi ametumia mbinu ya kejeli, akiandika methali hiyo kwa kuipindua; badala ya kusema “Subira huvuna waliokomaa,” ameandika “Subira huvuna waliokorofisha.” Haya yote yalikuwa ili kuonyesha huzuni ya mhusika huyu, Okello. 1.2.7 Nahau  
Mhusika BIBI anauliza swali kwa watu ambao wanaonekana kumuabudu Mungu kila siku, lakini matendo yao yamejaa dhuluma na uonevu mkubwa. Matendo wanayofanya hayaakisi mafundisho ya Mungu Mwenyezi. Wanatesa watu, watumwa, na mtu mwingine yeyote anayekutana nao ambaye hana rangi sawa ya ngozi nao. Swali hili kwa kweli ni kejeli inayolengwa kwa wale wanaoonekana kumuogopa Mungu huku wakitenda maovu. Mwandishi anasema, Mungu hadhihakiwi, hadanganywi, wala hababaishwi. Haya ni matamshi mafupi ambayo yanatumiwa na wanajamii kusisitiza ukweli wa jambo fulani. Inasemekana kwamba matamshi kama haya yanaunganisha dhana au mawazo tofauti katika hoja moja kwa lengo la kufikisha ujumbe uliokusudiwa. Ndani ya tamthilia iliyochaguliwa, *Sadaka ya John Okello*, mwandishi ametumia misemo mbalimbali. Kwa mfano;

Mwandishi ametumia maneno haya kutambulisha nadharia mbalimbali zilizotoa mwongozo kwa harakati katika jamii za Ulaya, na kuwawezesha watu kufikia ukombozi wa kweli. BABU anaeleza kwamba ikiwa watu watazielewa nadharia hizi zote, basi wataweza kufanya mapinduzi wanayoyatarajia kuyafanya. Nairobi: JKF. 1.3 Maoni na Mapendekezo  
Mwandishi wetu, Emmanuel Mbogo, ametumia lugha kwa ustadi mkubwa katika uandishi wa tamthilia hii. Kuanzia mwanzo hadi mwisho, msomaji anavutwa na kazi hii kwa namna ya kipekee. Ubunifu unaoelezwa na wanamitindo wa nadharia ya kimuundo umejitokeza waziwazi katika kazi hii. Kwa kuwa lugha imetumiwa kwa ufanisi, ujumbe uliokusudiwa bila shaka utaifikia hadhira. Endeleza ujuzi huu zaidi. 1.4 Hitimisho  
Fasihi ni tawi la sanaa linalotumia lugha ya mazungumzo au maandishi kuwasilisha ujumbe kwa jamii. Ili ujumbe uliokusudiwa uwafikie wanajamii kwa ufanisi, ni muhimu kwa waandishi kutumia lugha kwa ubunifu katika kufikisha ujumbe huo kwa hadhira. Emmanuel Mbogo ni mkazi wa Tanzania Bara, na tamthilia aliyoandika inahusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Lafudhi zilizotolewa kwa wahusika wote katika kazi hii kwa kiasi kikubwa zinaendana na za wakaazi wa visiwa hivyo. Kila anapoongea mhusika Mwarabu, lugha inamtambulisha. Mzaliwa wa Unguja anapoongea, lugha pia inamtambulisha. Mtumwa kutoka bara, ambaye ni sehemu ya msafara wa watumwa kutoka Tabora, anapoongea, lugha inamtambulisha pia. Wahusika wote wamepewa lugha inayoendana na majukumu yao. Vipengele vyote vilivyotumika vimeibua mada mbalimbali; mwandishi hakuvitumia kwa bahati mbaya. Sifa hizi za kilugha zililenga kuonesha mada tofauti ndani ya tamthilia hii. Hakika, misingi ya nadharia ya ustrukturalizimu

discourses.source_txt: The linguistic elements encompass all the fundamental contents used in literary works. The use of language is considered one of the artistic aspects of a literary work, and art contains all the essential components employed to create a literary piece, such as themes, characters, structure, style, and title. In the aspect of language use, critics examine these features—expressions, metaphors, foreign languages, and so on—depending on the critic's objective.

discourses.source_txt:
Introduction  
The use of language is one of the aspects found in the external structure of a literary work, that is, its form. Form encompasses all the essential elements used to shape a literary work, such as setting, characters, structure, style, and the title of the work/anthology, among others. In examining the use of language, critics focus on these elements: expressions, figures of speech, register, foreign languages, etc., depending on the critic’s objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the play *John Okello’s Sacrifice* (2015).

Matumizi ya lugha ni mojawapo ya mambo yanayopatikana katika muundo wa nje wa kazi ya fasihi, yaani umbo lake. Umbo linajumuisha vipengele vyote muhimu vinavyotumiwa kuunda kazi ya fasihi, kama vile muktadha, wahusika, muundo, mtindo, na kichwa cha kazi/antolojia, pamoja na mambo mengine. Katika kuchunguza matumizi ya lugha, wakosoaji huzingatia vipengele hivi: usemi, tamathali za semi, rejista, lugha za kigeni, n.k., kulingana na madhumuni ya mkosoaji. discourses.source_txt:
1.1 The Theory of Formalism  
Schmitz (2007) and Carter (2006) have outlined several ideas of formalist theorists as follows: distinguishing between the use of ordinary language and literary language, they believed and emphasized that the concept of innovation or novelty is the main function of art, and they preferred literary criticism to have a scientific orientation; thus, they sought to establish scientific approaches in literature.  
According to the ideas of the formalists, all literary works utilize this theory because a work cannot be considered literary if it does not possess artistic qualities. These artistic qualities involve the construction of language elements that demonstrate the novelty of the work. Therefore, anyone who critiques any literary work based on the theory of Formalism will inevitably have to confront the issue of "novelty"—that is, the features that construct the use of language are unavoidable. The theory of Formalism is among the theories that analyze and explain the use of language in the disciplines of literature and linguistics. This theory originated from activists in two academic circles in Russia: on the one hand, the linguists of the Moscow Linguistics Circle, and on the other, the Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), both aiming to bring revolutions to linguistics and literary criticism (Schmitz, 2007).
discourses.translated_txt:
1.1 Nadharia ya Uformali  
Schmitz (2007) na Carter (2006) wameelezea mawazo kadhaa ya wananadharia wa uformali kama ifuatavyo: kutofautisha kati ya matumizi ya lugha ya kawaida na lugha ya kifasihi, waliamini na kusisitiza kwamba dhana ya ubunifu au jambo jipya ndiyo kazi kuu ya sanaa, na walipendelea uchambuzi wa fasihi uwe na mwelekeo wa kisayansi; kwa hivyo, walilenga kuweka mbinu za kisayansi ndani ya fasihi.  
Kwa mujibu wa mawazo ya waformali, kazi zote za fasihi hutumia nadharia hii kwa sababu kazi haiwezi kuchukuliwa kuwa ya kifasihi kama haina sifa za kisanii. Sifa hizi za kisanii zinahusisha uundaji wa vipengele vya lugha vinavyoonyesha ubunifu wa kazi hiyo. Hivyo, mtu yeyote anayechambua kazi yoyote ya fasihi kwa msingi wa Nadharia ya Uformali hatakosa kukutana na suala la “ubunifu”—yaani, mambo yanayojenga matumizi ya lugha hayaepukiki. Nadharia ya Uformali ni miongoni mwa nadharia zinazochambua na kufafanua matumizi ya lugha katika taaluma za fasihi na isimu. Nadharia hii ilianzia kwa wanaharakati wa vikundi viwili vya kitaaluma nchini Urusi: kwa upande mmoja, wasomi wa Isimu kutoka Mduara wa Isimu wa Moscow, na kwa upande mwingine, Jumuiya ya Utafiti wa Lugha ya Ushairi (OPAYAZ), vyote vikilenga kuleta mapinduzi katika isimu na uchambuzi wa fasihi (Schmitz, 2007).

discourses.source_txt: In conclusion, the theory of Formalism has greatly contributed to the advancement and development of literary criticism. This contribution stems from the concept of innovation or novelty in literary works, the challenges and various debates it has sparked, which have generated diverse knowledge and ideas within the field of literature, as well as the emergence of other theories such as the theory of Modernism.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa kumalizia, nadharia ya Uformali imechangia kwa kiasi kikubwa katika ustawi na maendeleo ya ukosoaji wa fasihi. Mchango huu unatokana na dhana ya ubunifu au jipya katika kazi za fasihi, changamoto na mijadala mbalimbali ilizozusha, ambazo zimesababisha kujitokeza kwa maarifa na mawazo tofauti tofauti katika uwanja wa fasihi, pamoja na kujitokeza kwa nadharia nyingine kama vile nadharia ya Uhamiaji wa Kisasa (Modernism).

discourses.source_txt: According to Carter (2006), the concept of habitualization arises when something is used repeatedly to the point that it becomes automatic. In literature, habitualization can occur if the reader or listener perceives a literary work as ordinary and fails to distinguish it from a non-literary (ordinary) work. This results from hearing or reading the work repeatedly.

1.3 Comments and Recommendations  
Our author, Emmanuel Mbogo, has made excellent use of language in the construction of this play. From the beginning to the end, the reader is continually engaged with this work. The innovation described by structuralists in theory truly manifests itself in this work.
discourses.translated_txt:
1.3 Maoni na Mapendekezo  
Mwandishi wetu, Emmanuel Mbogo, ametumia lugha kwa ustadi mkubwa katika uandishi wa tamthilia hii. Kuanzia mwanzo hadi mwisho, msomaji anavutwa na kazi hii kwa namna ya kipekee. Ubunifu unaoelezwa na wanamitindo wa nadharia ya kimuundo umejitokeza waziwazi katika kazi hii.

1.4 Conclusion  
Literature is a branch of art that uses spoken or written language to convey a message to society. For the intended message to reach the community effectively, it is important for writers to use language creatively in delivering that message to the audience.
discourses.translated_txt:
1.4 Hitimisho  
Fasihi ni tawi la sanaa linalotumia lugha ya mazungumzo au maandishi kuwasilisha ujumbe kwa jamii. Ili ujumbe uliokusudiwa uwafikie wanajamii kwa ufanisi, ni muhimu kwa waandishi kutumia lugha kwa ubunifu katika kufikisha ujumbe huo kwa hadhira.

discourses.source_txt: Emmanuel Mbogo is a resident of mainland Tanzania, and the play he wrote concerns the people of Zanzibar (Unguja and Pemba). The accents given to all the characters in this work largely match those of the island inhabitants. When an Arab character speaks, the language identifies him. When a native of Unguja speaks, the language identifies him as well. When a slave from the mainland, part of a caravan of slaves from Tabora, speaks, the language also identifies him.
discourses.translated_txt: Emmanuel Mbogo ni mkazi wa Tanzania Bara, na tamthilia aliyoandika inahusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Lafudhi zilizotolewa kwa wahusika wote katika kazi hii kwa kiasi kikubwa zinaendana na za wakaazi wa visiwa hivyo. Kila anapoongea mhusika Mwarabu, lugha inamtambulisha. Mzaliwa wa Unguja anapoongea, lugha pia inamtambulisha. Mtumwa kutoka bara, ambaye ni sehemu ya msafara wa watumwa kutoka Tabora, anapoongea, lugha inamtambulisha pia.
